name: Yukon
summary: Green, white and blue vertical bands with the territory's coat of arms in the white centre, over a wreath of fireweed, the territorial flower.
origin: The flag was chosen in a 1967 competition for Canada's centennial and designed by Lynn Lambert, a librarian. It was adopted on 1 March 1968.

symbols.name: Coat of arms
symbols.description: A shield with St George's Cross, a roundel of vair (fur), wavy lines and mountains, with a malamute dog on top.
symbols.meaning: British heritage, the fur trade, the Yukon River and mineral-rich mountains.

symbols.name: Fireweed
symbols.description: A wreath of purple fireweed flowers.

facts: The malamute represents the dog-sled heritage of the Klondike.
The Klondike Gold Rush of 1896–1899 brought tens of thousands to the territory.
Its centre band is wider than the outer bands.
clues: Green, white and blue vertical bands with a coat of arms above purple flowers.
Its arms are topped by a sled dog.
Its territory saw a famous gold rush.
